verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of PDF page 860 (printed page 838, Index) shows a two-level and sometimes three-level index hierarchy. Sub-entries are visibly indented under their headwords: ALPHABETIC phrase > CLASS clause 269 and INITIALIZE statement 457; Alphabet-name > CODE-SET clause 271 and others; Archaic language elements > Continuation of COBOL words 833 and others; and Alphabetic class > Class of data > Alphabetic 111 at three levels. In page-860.md every line carries the same 3-space prefix and a trailing backslash. The only lines that keep indentation are ' Alphabetic 111' and the wrap continuation '  meric items 833'. As a result, headword and sub-entry lines cannot be told apart: 'CLASS clause 269' reads as a top-level entry. This loses the parent/child relationship, which is index content, not just wrapping or furniture. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The page is the non-normative index, so this does not affect normative text.
